text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- (Right wing) Disy party vice chairman Nicos Anastassiades appeals for unity in the party as he announces his intention to run for the post of party chairman at elections.
- The labour ministry says the unemployment rate is contained at 3.1 percent and this is expected to fall during the course of the year.
- President Glafcos Clerides is to get a 29 percent pay rise under a supplementary budget tabled in parliament.
- Paphos MPs say the local hospital is "critically ill."
- Kurds threaten to step up their fight against Turkish interests.

- The structured dialogue between Cyprus and the European Union comes up against a new hitch from the insistence of Britain and Germany for the involvement of Turkish Cypriots in accession negotiations.
- Nicos Anastassiades announces his intention to run for the post of Disy chairman.
- Turkey shuts the door on developments on Cyprus, ruling out any switch in Ankara's policy on the Cyprus issue.
- Provocative payrises. The finance ministry suggests a 29 percent pay rise to the president, the president of parliament and to ministers.
